# kode-gopher: how to write Go for the execute_go_code MCP tool

You have access to the `execute_go_code` MCP tool. It builds and runs Go code in a sandboxed Kubernetes pod (gVisor-isolated on GKE, runsc-free on local kind) and returns a structured result. You also have `gcp_auth_status` (report the sandbox's credential identity) and `lookup_package_docs` (fetch godoc for curated packages).

## Prewarmed curated packages

The sandbox image ships a prewarmed `$GOCACHE` + `$GOMODCACHE` for exactly this set of packages plus their transitive deps:

  cloud.google.com/go/storage
  cloud.google.com/go/compute/apiv1
  cloud.google.com/go/container/apiv1
  cloud.google.com/go/bigquery
  cloud.google.com/go/secretmanager/apiv1
  google.golang.org/api/option
  k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1
  k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes
  k8s.io/client-go/tools/clientcmd
  k8s.io/client-go/dynamic
  k8s.io/client-go/tools/watch

Snippets that import only these packages build in ~5 seconds. Anything else triggers `go mod tidy` on first use — slower and may re-tidy shared transitives, invalidating the compile cache.

Use `lookup_package_docs` to check a function signature or method set from any curated package without paying an `execute_go_code` round-trip.

## Two input shapes

**Single-file** (`code` arg): pass Go source as a string. Choose one of:

1. **Snippet mode (recommended)**. Any package name other than `main`. Declare exactly:
   ```go
   func run(ctx context.Context) (any, error)
   ```
   Your return value is JSON-marshaled into `result.value`. Errors and panics land as `result.kind=error` / `result.kind=panic`. The wrapper provides `func main()` — don't write one.

2. **Full program mode**. `package main` with `func main()`. Your code owns stdout/stderr. If you want a structured result, write JSON to `/app/.kode-gopher/result.json` before exiting.

**Multi-file** (`files` arg): pass a `map[string]string` keyed by path. Root files (no `/`) form the entry-point package. Subdirectory files are separate helper packages. The synthesized module name is `kode_gopher_user`, so a helper at `helper/util.go` is imported as `kode_gopher_user/helper`.

## Credentials

Google Cloud calls authenticate via forwarded Application Default Credentials — the sandbox's identity is whoever ran `gcloud auth application-default login` on the host. Call `gcp_auth_status` to confirm the identity + project before consequential API calls.

Environment: `$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` is forwarded into the run phase. ADC lands at `/app/.kode-gopher/creds/adc.json` and `$GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` points at it.

## Kubernetes API access

For the sandbox's OWN cluster: `rest.InClusterConfig()` works — the pod's KSA token is mounted. The default KSA has no RBAC bindings; typed calls (Pods().List, etc.) will 403 unless a Role is granted.

For OTHER GKE clusters: use `container/apiv1` `ListClusters`/`GetCluster` to find the cluster, prefer `c.ControlPlaneEndpointsConfig.DnsEndpointConfig.Endpoint` over `c.Endpoint` (the DNS endpoint routes through Google's control plane, works for private-endpoint clusters, uses system-trust TLS), and wrap an `oauth2.Transport` sourced from `google.DefaultTokenSource` as `rest.Config.WrapTransport`.

## Failure surfaces

The tool returns `phase` (build/run), `exit_code`, `stdout`, `stderr`, and `result` (kind + value/message/stack). `IsError` is true when either the program crashed or `result.kind != "ok"`.
